profile.address: South Lincoln Avenue, Clayville, Vineland, Cumberland County, New Jersey, 08361
profile.reading:
This site in the Clayville section of Vineland, in Cumberland County, New Jersey, is under construction as one of the largest data-center commitments Nebius has made in the United States. Nebius is the AI-infrastructure and cloud-computing company that emerged from Yandex N.V., the Amsterdam-registered international arm of the Russian search company Yandex, after Yandex N.V. sold its Russian operations in 2024 and rebranded the remaining international business as Nebius Group.

The project is a build-to-suit arrangement: DataOne, a data center developer, owns and will operate the physical building, with Nebius signed on as the anchor tenant that will fill it with GPU infrastructure. Nebius announced the New Jersey commitment in March 2025 as part of a broader U.S. expansion that also added capacity in Kansas City, describing design capacity for the New Jersey site at up to 300 megawatts, developed in phases, with the company targeting its first 100 megawatts of installed capacity by the end of 2025 and the site fully operational by 2027. Company materials describe roughly 200 permanent on-site jobs once operational and about 1,000 construction jobs during the build, with a stated goal that 90 percent of the workforce be drawn locally - DataOne has said it expects to become one of the largest taxpayers in South Jersey once the facility is generating tax revenue.

The power strategy is unusual among data centers in this registry: rather than drawing incremental load from the regional grid, Nebius has partnered with Bloom Energy to generate power on site using solid-oxide fuel cells, an arrangement the companies describe as effectively off-grid, with no impact on residential ratepayers' electricity costs and classification as a minor source under air-permitting rules. Cooling is designed as a closed-loop system, with a one-time fill requirement of about one million gallons of water and estimated annual consumption on the order of several million gallons, equivalent to roughly seven Olympic swimming pools, most of which the companies attribute to office rather than cooling use. The building shell itself is being built by Northeast Precast, a Vineland-based construction firm, giving the project a regional supply-chain component alongside its hyperscale tenant.

Nebius and DataOne have also announced a community-benefits program tied to the site, including K-12 STEM and AI-literacy programming, GPU access grants, career-readiness training run with Rowan University and regional trade schools, and support for local first responders and emergency preparedness. As of this writing the facility remains under construction, with capacity being brought online in phases rather than delivered all at once, so figures describing capacity should be read as targets on a multi-year build-out rather than as a completed project.
